label: late copy-phase steps (recall index >= 5, or final step of L=3) on certain input tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>. Activity is concentrated late in the copy: recall_idx >= 5 (rate ~35%, about 7x lift), plus the final output step of L=3 sequences, where the largest activations occur (many top examples are the last copy step of L=3, e.g. q b k <DEL> q [b]). Within the timing window it is graded by the input token: h, m, 3, x, b, i fire most often (about 73% precision), then p, o, l, 0, 1, v, while other tokens rarely fire. The timing window alone covers 96% of activation mass but only 35% precision. Adding the 12-token set gives dev F1 0.61 and mass recall 0.73. The token preference is graded, not a clean set, so it is only partially explained. Rate goes up toward the last steps (to_go 0-1 hold about 82% of mass). Does not fire at recall_idx 0-1 or at the first occurrence of any token.
